newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks edge higher at open, resources star.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks edge higher at open, resources star.

text.p: Australian shares opened modestly firmer on Friday with investors content to pick up stock in major resource issues after offshore markets provided few leads on Thursday.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.2 points firmer at 2,418.4.
The June share price index was just one point higher at 2,414 and at a 4.4 point discount to the underlying index.
Bank of Melbourne Ltd was the most active stock early with three large trades put through the market at the start of trade, the largest by Merril Lynch.
A Melbourne dealer said it was possible some investors were still concerned that Westpac Banking Corp's A$1.4 billion bid for Bank of Melbourne could be blocked by the monopolies regulator.
"There are a few bargain hunters around in the resources sector which has been oversold recently," said Martin Angel, a dealer at Perth brokerage Eyres Reed.

Angel said local investors could have been factoring in a 2.2 percent rise for the large gold sector on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday. "There is not a lot of trade going on - not a lot of sell orders coming in," Angel said.
Amongst the better performing issues were Australia's largest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and base metal group MIM Holdings Ltd whose shares were four cents higher at A$1.69 (US$1.31).
Oil and gas issues were mostly firmer with Woodside Petroleum Ltd recovering more than half of its fall on Thursday after it fell on a disappointing drilling result.
Woodside shares were 20 cents higher at A$9.75.
Another strong oil company was Papua New Guinea explorer and producer, Oilsearch Ltd whose shares were up 12 cents at A$3.06 on good volume.
"The company (Oil Search) is up on speculation of a good result from a Papua New Guinea well, which is close to its target depth," a Brisbane-based dealer said.
